angle: Sitting down and stopping. The out-breath running longer than the in-breath. Nothing required of the body for the next while.
The small physical unclenchings: jaw, shoulders, hands opening in the lap, the face going slack. Permission to stop holding things up.
Weight arriving. The chair taking the whole body. Limbs getting heavy and pleasantly hard to move.
Narrowing and the eyes. One spot, one word, edges going soft, blinking slower, lids too heavy to lift.
Threshold-crossing motion: stairs down, a slope, sinking, counting down, the descent continuing on its own without effort.
Fully across. Sound receding, the room further away, the body distant and warm, one slow thought at a time.
First stirrings. Fingers and toes moving again, a breath drawn on purpose, the chair felt under the body.
The room coming back near. Sound arriving close again, light behind the lids, the edges sharpening.
Mid-climb. Counting up, rising toward the surface, sensation flooding the arms and legs, a stretch running through.
Eyes getting ready and opening. Blinking clear, the lids lifting easily, vision steady and bright.
Fully out and alert. Wide awake, rested, clear-headed, steady, present in the room and ready for the rest of the day.
Integration. What settled stays settled with the eyes open, carried out of the chair into the day, awake and changed rather than awake and blank.
